title: Sins of a Solar Empire®: Rebellion
text: Greetings as always!  Let us get to my next review, Sins of Solar Empire:  Rebellion.  If you have been following my reviews at all you know that I have a weakness for RTS, especially those with depth and expansions.  How does this game compare?  Well to start I have almost 120 hours played and 100% unlock achievement wise…so what do you think?  Anyway Review time! Lane Jumping:  This game is one of my top RTS to play (alongside the StarCraft Series and the Dawn of War Series), with that said it has some very well done differences.  To begin with the game is designed to be played at a more macro level:  everything from ship-management to research can be done while zoomed out; creating a massive suite of quality of life features, especially shift commands which I find essential in an RTS.  The base line of the game is a space faring real time strategy where you colonize planets that are separated by phase lanes, which are warp points that separate the planets gravity wells.  The idea being that only gravity wells inhibit phase jumps and are really the only things worth fighting over (for the sake of this asteroids, space stations, even stars are planets).  You do a light amount of management of the planets but they act more like a new resource point and less like a planet to govern.  Finally, you can build capital ships that level up and have special abilities.  All this done fully zoomed out or so close you can see your individual fighters flying around. Benny Hill Time:  The game does have some minor flaws however; one of the biggest is the AI’s overwhelming need to run away from any fight if they have less than a 99% chance of winning.  In most RTS the enemy will send probing attack at you from time to time and depending on the RTS in question they may eventually retreat.  But, they will always come in and at least try to attack.  The AI in Sins will run away immediately when it does some background calculation stating that it would lose the battle.  It doesn’t matter if it has reinforcements coming and only needs to hold you up or this is their capital planet.  Amusingly (and annoyingly) they sometimes get caught in a weird loop where they warp out then come right back and continue doing this until they have the forces to overwhelm you or you slowly kill their entire fleet by staying near the phase lane.  This by far is biggest annoyance of this entire game that and… Narratives in Space:  This game, like many well thought out RTS have an amazing narrative with an interesting back-story, unfortunately that is where it ends.  I love this game so much and would pay for an entirely new game for just a single player campaign.  But alas, nope… However, where the game fails in a story the narrative is really good.  The ships have voice over’s and even the research you can do allude to a bit of story between the factions.  In addition to that the games art style is amazing including realistic ship designs with a diverse amount of weapon types and sound effects.  The game does tend to do a bit of cookie-cutter in the ways of the roles of the ships where the placement of the ship in the build menus tends to serve the same role as the other factions but they still feel unique in their methods and even abilities.  Oh, and the fact that ships behave like they should (kind of hard to dodge in a big capital ship) is really great, seeing these big fleets line up to shoot while hundreds of little fighters and bombers flying about is amazing. As I’m sure you have seen I spent a fair bit more time telling you what I don’t like instead of what I do.  I want to be clear, if you love RTS this game should be in your library.  This is why I seem to have a bit of a negative look at it; tis another game so close to perfection it hurts.  So, do I recommend?  You bet I do!  Just do a Google search to change how to make AI stop being such cowards and / or play with human friends.  Up to you, enjoy!

title: Sins of a Solar Empire®: Rebellion
text: Let's start with the 4x elements first. There is almost no planetary development. You can grow population, add some slots for buildings, improve your planet's health all with a couple of clicks. It will take a few minutes to fully develope your planet. The research tree is generic. When you build let's say a frigate factory you will unlock one ship type. There is a research tab for every ship in the game for unlock only purpose.  There are 4 tabs alone for upgrading armor, doing the same thing for every tab. Same thing for laser weapons, 3 tabs where every tab is divided into 2 levels ( need to research 1 tab twice) for every incremental increase in laser damage. There is so much unnecessary stuff in the tree that it is just not tech tree worthy as a whole. Expansion is pretty straightforward take a planet by force or take it over by influence. Panets are connected by phase lanes (strings) over which are you able to move and spread your influence. I'd say diplomacy is the only 4x worthy element this game has to offer and worked out well. You can accept missions to increase their relation with you or you give them a mission to improve your relation with them. If the relation in both ways is high enough the chance of them accepting heavier stuff is more probable. You may ask (missions) a faction to destroy ships, capital ships, structures etc and the amount of it. If they kill 5 or 15 enemy ships for you depends on the relationship. You are also able to join pacts. The better the relation, the more pacts you can join like cease fire, peace, vision or trade treaties. Managing your economy is just as thin as in any other RTS, colonize asteroids for metal and crystal income and max out your population for credits. First of all there is no singleplayer campaign, it is just pure skirmish against bots and multiplayer. Second point I want to make is that the majority of your game time is spend by battling enemy fleets. Gameplay wise you build up a fleet of mixed unit types. Attack the enemy, lose a big chunk of your fleet, rebuild your fleet and go for the next planet. Flanking does not pay off. There isn't any tactics involved other than timing the activation of your ship's special abilities. There is no stealth, no surgical strikes, no flanking. Every game plays out the same, build a big balanced fleet and overwhelm the enemy. Quick building is your way to succes. This is a casual RTS game with extra bells and whistles (4x elements) which lacks strategic depth. The game has good graphics and the battles are nice to see when you are zoomed in, which rarely happens anyway. I did not expect this game to have such a lack of tactical gameplay, such a shame. For a casual RTS experience this game is good. Good graphics, flashy space battles, lots of cool units, wonderful sound effects, always things to do, mods and the 4x elements , altough very minor, are a plus. I would not buy the game if you expect a 4x game, total war style of gameplay or the ability to use tactics to decide battles. I would only recommend this game if you want another casual RTS experience (with casual I don't mean quality, but there are more of them on the market in terms of gameplay). I will give this game thumbs down however (has nothing to do with rating but with recommendation), the reason for downvoting is the lack of depth gameplay wise and the bells an whistles don't make up for it.

title: Slain: Back from Hell
text: Is this game a joke? When you hitting repeatedly the attack button and then hit the jump button, what do you expect? Hm? Nothing? Correct! Because this is what happens: nothing! When you hit the attack button twice or ten times in the air, what do you expect? Correct! Only one single hit! One SINGLE hit! Because... why? When you come down, after a jump, you can't attack for a second or so! Again... why? Do you know the situation, where you want to jump from the edge of a cliff, but instead fall off? Yes, this is the kind of game. In this game it's all about timing, as if you going to win a fighting beauty contest or something. The same type of enemy can have different attack timings. You think you can hit it twice, but... nope, this one shoots earlier. Until you learn all the patterns and all the tricks, you repeatedly play the same passage over and over again. When you finaly manage to pass it, you don't have the feeling you did it with you SKILL, but because you just KNOW all the movements of your enemy. You basically predict the future, which is absolutly unsatisfying. If you step in blood, you die. Because... why??? Or is it lava...? PS: Oh, yes the soundtrack: it's a short tune playing over and over. I wouldn't call it a track. Or was it because I died so many times and had to listen to the same short part repeatedly? Anyway I switched it off. Then you hear some ambient sound, like wind, which is good and atmospheric (not like the music!).

title: Slain: Back from Hell
text: I would say that is NES hard but that would not give it justice. The difficulty is not exactly fair and frankly, the game mechanics like counter-hit and block are not very reliable. METAL music and Pixel art is top of the line but if you can't play beat the level, you won't see a whole lot of the game. Platforming elements are lacking so you just gonna mash buttons and hope all that cluster-**** on the screen does not kill you. I can't classify it as a bad game but if you have no tolerance for BS difficulty you probably won't enjoy it. Man the achievements for this game. "Beat the game without Dying" which only 0.1% of players have after presumably 5000+ people who played the game. Basically, the developer made a joke and nobody gonna get completion for this game. You will have better luck beating Battletoads blindfolded. It is not much of a platformer. All you have is a basic jump and a back-dash which does not give much mobility. 90% of the game is the just timing your attack and counter-hit. Hope you can kill them before they kill you. There are some secret areas but for the most part, the game is rather linear. Even though the game is focused on combat that part is also lacking, to say the least. Aside from basic attack, you have charged attack which is too slow for the pace of the game. You will get some powerups such as different weapons that deal extra damage to specific enemies ( and...they don't really change how you play ) Overall pretty generic mechanics and not all that interesting. Skill in the game is mostly gained by trial and error instead of good judgment. Usually, there are too many enemies on the screen to apply any strategy on the go. You will mostly progress by dying over and over until you know exactly what to do. There are some beginner traps but you can spot them visually. It may not seem like a big problem until enemies start to bounce you back into instadeath spots. One of the sections in the game took me maybe 40+ respawns and was the only level 2. It is kinda like birds in Castlevania feeling multiplied by 3. Since the game has a lot of tedious button mashing, restarting the same section over and over is not particularly fun. Checkpoints can be pretty unforgiving. It seems like the game always wants to push it one step too far out of your comfort zone. In some spots, I am not even sure if it is possible to avoid damage. Like you are completely surrounded by enemies with a bunch of projectiles coming from both sides. The only solution sometimes is to take few hits on purpose and get to one side of the screen. So the game teaches you to use block which by the way has extremely poor consistency in the game. Some of the regular enemies, go right through with no indication. Even if you do block the damage reduction is abysmal. I find it easier to either avoid close combat completely or rely on charge/counter hit. Counter-Hit is the name of the game. You need it to get through many big enemies but even if I time it to animation it just works 33% of the time. It depends on the enemy but you cannot rely on the damn thing even though you have to do it consistently throughout the game. This is one thing that game does flawlessly. Some of the coolest pixel gore in the business but it might be hard to enjoy aesthetics when the game requires so much focus. Everything has a METAL theme which makes constant deaths appropriate. I like the occasional boobies, very nice touch. Animations look great and there is a good variety of enemies and levels.I also like the small story bits and interactions between characters. I generally do not hold the difficulty against the game but it could use some "difficulty settings". The gameplay depth is not even that deep or unique in any way. The saving grace for me and the only reason I can recommend it is the fantastic pixel art. Hard games are fun when frustration is balanced by fun gameplay but here you get a lot of frustration and a lot of tedious repetition.

title: Slain: Back from Hell
text: Slain is a rare success story in the sense that it released in horrific condition and instead of washing their hands of it and cashing what little money they made from it the devs actually fixed it, and so we have Slain: Back from Hell which is basically version 2.0 and it fixes most of the issues that plagued initial release build, which is reflected in the recent (very positive) and overall (mixed) scores in the Steam user reviews section. I'd like to start off by saying Slain is hard, almost frustratingly so at times so you're going to die, a lot. Going into the game I didn't quite understand how challenging it was meant to be so it was quite the shock. Just for reference I have finished Bloodborne, the Dark Souls series and Salt & Sanctuary so I'm no stranger to hard games but Slain had a way of making me feel like it was being unnecessarily hard or even cheap just for the sake of it at times, however for the most part the game was a solid, enjoyable challenge, it's just a shame the overall experience was tarnished a little due to a few rare outliers that left me saying to myself "Really?.....", for example certain mobs have brutally tight timings on their counter attack, and when you have to hit multiple of them in a row without taking a single hit it can be frustrating, and it was. I also found myself begging to the Metal Gods themselves for a checkpoint at times after a tough section or mob but was left wanting which again caused frustration when I died and had to do it all again. I'd like to make it clear though, for the most part this isn't an issue, but these blips really did hurt my enjoyment of the game and I think Slain would benefit greatly from a final tuning phase. Difficulty aside the game is tight for the most part, but I did run into a couple of issues where my attacks would pass through enemies, most notably on the final boss, I also had an issue where the charge up attack would sometimes cancel before the *ching* even though I was holding down the button still, it didn't happen a lot but enough to become very frustrating, especially as it often meant death when it occurred. Other than those issues the gameplay is good, the controls feel responsive and the combat is enjoyable, I would highly recommend using the D-Pad over the thumb sticks, though, as it was far more accurate IMO. Technically I had no issues, I played the game on a GTX 970 / 3570k @ 4.3GHz and it ran at a solid 60fps throughout on maximum settings which is what you'd expect, but it's not always the case sadly so I thought I'd mention it. Visually the game is great and I say that as someone who isn't a big fan of pixel/retro style graphics but in Slain's case they worked and were executed well. To go with the smart visuals we also have a solid metal soundtrack which is a core part of the game and theme, so it was crucial that it was good and it is. Overall I do recommend the game but only if you enjoy challenging games, if you go into Slain expecting to He-man your way through everything you'll be sorely disappointed, you never feel particularly powerful and you're always one wrong button press away from death so it's quite stressful, but if this sort of adrenaline rush is what you enjoy then I'm sure you'll have a blast with Slain: Back from Hell. 6/10

title: Slain: Back from Hell
text: I love Metal I love Pixels I come from the 80s Thus, Slain seemed like it would be right up my alley, and although I’m enjoying it so far, it does sometimes leave me a bit on the salty side The Goods Atmosphere and Graphics:  This is the best pixel art I’ve seen in a long time.  Imagine all your favourite Iron Maiden, Slayer and Death album covers having a massive orgy on your SNES after popping enough A class to down a wilder beast -  its that bloomin’ good, but it has a really dirty and scratched style to it that only enhances the metal vibe.  Plenty of boobies and plenty of blood!  Great animations and lighting effects too Controls: overall pretty tight and responsive.  I love parrying and riposting Sound effects: proper 80s and very crunchy Gameplay:  when the game is at its best, it is an absolute blast to play, a blast out of the 16 bit past with all its 2d gameplay glory, and makes you feel like a titanic bad♥♥♥♥♥when you land a parry on a boss The annoyances Cheapness:  OMG this game ican be cheaper than an email scammer who has £3m inheritance for you and just needs your ALL bank details so they can send it along.  It regularly spawns enemies right on top of you( enemies damage on touch) or lets baddies shoot you from off screen and all manner of below the belt play.  Whereas something like Dark Souls of Hyper Light Drifter is difficult and challenging, Slain can be so cheap Pacing:  This game is at its best when it lets you keep a high pace, such as the wolf parts or the earlier levels.  However, it often forces you to play the same room/section over and over again because you keep dying – the levels are actually quite small and it gets repetitive. Music – I am an uber metal fan (1000 albums plus yo), and the music was what originally drew me to this game.  However, while the music sounds sweone for the first 30 seconds (damn i love that raw guitar sound) it gets too repetitive, with the same simple riffs over and over again.  I wasn’t expecting Borknargar, but I was expecting better than this (well at least this is better than cold lake eh Curt?).  Actually I think I’ll put some Bork on in the background instead. OVERALL Lads n lassies, at the end of the day, this was well worth the £5 I paid for it. The art is astounding, I loved the 1980s boobs and demons vibe, and when the game is rollicking a long at a good pace it is brilliant, almost like a pre SOTN castlevania.  However, while it does 80s action platformer, it doesn’t bring anything new to the table, and it can throw a lot of cheap shots at you. Not one of my top picks this year, but definitely not a bad game all in all

title: Slain: Back from Hell
text: Nope, nope, as much as I wanted to like this game, just NOPE. It looks fantastic but it plays like crap. I have been looking forward to Slain!'s release for about 9 months hoping it would become a new Castlevania title. But now, after the release date got postponed several times, the game still feels incredibly unfinished and poorly coded: - most sound effects are MISSING (like in THEY ARE NOT THERE AT ALL) - metal soundtrack is repetitive - controls are sluggish and delayed (which makes you die hundreds of times and contributes to massive frustration and full metal rage quits), no matter if you are playing with M+K or controller - dialogs look like they have been (mis-)translated from Chinese to English resulting in numerous spelling errors, weird grammar, or they just make no sense - difficulty is ridiculously high (mostly due to the clunky controls mentioned above but also due to many instakill traps) Maybe if there were features like Double Jumps, Ledge Graps, Sprints, Weapon Upgrades, Usable Items and stuff like that the 'Metroidvania' tag would be justified, but in its current state I only see a pseudo game with great art style that basically lacks everything else. All in all, it's just no fun playing this game - despite the great looks - and that makes me sad.

title: Slain: Back from Hell
text: Initially funded this through Kickstarter when it was finally released I was super hyped and then very super disappointed. The first release was terrible. Delayed responsiveness, no exit option, no re-config of control heck it was a guessing game of what controls did what. An absolute mess and I was devastated. I stepped away and decided to give them some time (and feedback) to sort out the issues. Post Patch 1.0 This game is AMAZING! The music is phenomenal and sums up nicely all the things that was 80-90s arcade side scrolling level jumping barbarian metal. All the soundtracks are very metal and very appropriate. The art direction and style of the game is exactly what you\'d expect from a game that set out to be a 80s/90s arcade game. The controls are responsive and customizable. The menu has been fixed and any bugs from their initial release have been dealth with. I\'m very impressed they immediately fixed all the issues and can forgive the fact they released a flawed product due to the pressure they were 3+ months behind schedule but hey it\'s from an Indie studio and they did incredible as far as I\'m concerned. Well done Wolfbrew. Worth the cost and a fun game.

title: Slayaway Camp
text: It's kind of amazing how much depth can be put into a game with a cool concept and the will to do so. The game it's a simple puzzle game with a horror "slasher flick" type of theme attached to it, the idea is that your character can move in four directions, left, right, up, down, only that your character won't stop unless there's something blocking it's path, alternatively there can be traps, cops field's of view, or simply getting stuck in between a couple of blocks are the things that can end your run. The game also does sometimes without warning this cool "switch" of elements in the mechanics in some of the levels, (this ones presented as movies in vcr cassettes with cool covers and "previews" in the form of cutscenes always featuring different "killers" that you'll control during the remainer of the set of levels) The idea in most cases is simply to stay alive and kill all civilians in a level, sounds a bit dark for a game with such a "cartoony" and "cute" aesthetic, but in reality the game, while keeping it's tongue'in cheek a bit with it's mixture of humor and violence can at times borderline in brutality, whenever you... "Take out" any of your... "Targets" the game has a chance of displaying a cutscene, at times one that can be reproduced by frightening people away from you leading them into traps (fires, holes in the ground, water tombs filled with cocodriles, etc...) altho in most cases it will simply reproduce a random cutscene of a massive set of dozens of them that are quite characteristic and that can be multiplied repeatedly by spending coins that you earn in-game. At the end of each level (in a set of them) you can earn currency by completing a time event in a cutscene in which your character will be murdering an individual, then you'll earn "coins" that you can then spend either in more killers that you can select and use in the numerous of films/levels, or alternatively in more animations for the random executions that are displayed when murdering your "enemies". The game for the most part it's quite self-explanatory, and it has an almost perfect learning curve, I would compare it to something like Hitman Go, but I feel, as much as I love that game, this game has it's own unique aspects in it's core game design that need to be shared, and for good reason, most of them, even after attempting a level multiple times, never really frustrated me as muchs as in other game's "personal" failures, could have, Hitman Go being a perfect example of this. Instead the game offers a really cool "mechanic" to not call it "feature" that allows you to not only revert your mistakes resetting your position to the last movement you made, but also the ability to display handy tips for the shy price of just a couple of your in-game coins, if you still can't figure things out, after your second payment for tips, the solution for the level will be revealed. Overall i'm really pleased as well as surprised by the ammount of quality, and content there is for this game, it's an actual fleshed out release, and even then, the game feels as just another small, maybe kind of try, and see how it is, during a sale, type of title, lost within the vast Steam store library of games, I feel as if it doesn't only deserves more attention, as much as it deserves much more significant exposure on the part of the "marketing deparment" in itself, altho maybe there's not much it can be done to promote core gameplay aspects of a game that appears rather "simplistic" at first and yet internally, profoundly, it helds an amazing ammount of passion, and heart. Good ridance, good ridance indeed.

title: Slayaway Camp
text: This game is a really fun and very challenging puzzle game.  The graphics style is a blocky minecraft style, with hilarious over the top gory murder scenes.  The game is seperated into different stories which are reminiscent of old slasher films, and come with funny cutscenes at the start of each movie.  The difficulty curve is pretty well constructed.  The first few levels of each movie start out by teaching you about new mechanics and the rest of the levels make you learn how to use the new mechanics in an advanced way.  Since new game mechanics are introduced in each movie it keeps the gameplay from becoming boring.  If a level gets too difficult, you can ask for tips, or even have them show you how to do the level.  On the later levels you might need help because they get super complicated.  You can also spend the coins you earn to purchase gory executions and new killers to play as, which adds more replay value to the game.  After you've beaten a movie, you can go back and play the deleted scenes from each movie, and after you've played all the movies, you unlock special NC-17 levels, so there are tons and tons of levels for those puzzle maniacs out there. To summarize, this game has a hilarious atmosphere, lots of levels to play, and lots of things to unlock.

text: Total impulse buy. The game was on sale for cheap and I didn't even finish reading the description. Probably not the best method of purchasing a game,, but I lucked out. This is a puzzle game. Now, I normally don't play puzzle games, so I don't have the biggest library of game knowledge to compare this to, but it reminds me of a cross between Hitman Go and one of those flash games where you try to get the car out of a parking lot, or into a certain spot in a parking lot, etc.,. Each level is a static checkerboard, and pressing in any direction will send your character, the murderer, as far in that direction as he can possibly go. The result is that you have to shift your character around using the level layout in order to reach some harder to get to squares. The game teaches you the mechanics in the beginning tutorial and then gradually ramps up the difficulty as you progress, adding more enviromental factors and different types of NPCs. It's a very addictive game in and of itself, but there is a lot of homage to slasher films in here. Aside from the puzzle play trial and error (and don't worry - you can use in-game currency that you collect to unlock hints or answers in case you get stuck), the longevity comes from trying to collect two things: death scenes and different murderers. Fair warning, it takes quite a lot of grinding to collect enough coins to unlock all of these things, and that would be my only gripe with this game: after a few levels, you unlock a coin grinder mini-game. While this is certainly helpful compared to playing through a stage and collected coins, I do feel it doesn't give you enough coins. Each successful scene in the mini-game nets you 10 coins. All killers are 1,000 coins, and the death scenes range from a couple hundred to 2,500. The mini-game becomes difficult by the late teens, meaning even if you are able to score 20, you're only getting 200 coins. It got to the point where I played the final deleted scene of the final movie (campaign) over and over because it routinely nets you nearly 300 coins. Honestly, though, I think I stuck it out just to get all the steam achievements. That in and of itself is an accomplishment for the game, as I don't normally feel the need to play over and over for these. Overall, the game is a lot of fun, and if you're a fan of these type of puzzle games, I don't think you can go wrong. At only $9, with my 30 hours put in, that's essentially 30 cents an hour. I've averaged the total length of time a mainstream action title nets me at 12 hours. At $60, that's $5/hr., so do I think you'll get your money's worth with this game? Yes, absolutely. Even if you don't feel the need to grind out unlockables, it'll still come in at a better value if you put even two hours into this game.

title: Sleeping Dogs: Definitive Edition
text: I had a lot more fun with this game than I expected. It feels like a Japanese developer made a GTA style game set in China. Personally, I would focus on the main story missions, but there is actually a lot of side content. There are races you can take part in, and you can enter fighting tournaments. Lots of police side-missions too, but you really just need to focus on the Triad/Green missions on your map. I got probably 16-17 hours of play out of this game including some side stuff. That also includes the two extra DLC campaigns that come with the Definitive Edition. These are the Nightmare and Serpent options when you are on the main menu. You should play these after completing the main campaign in order not to spoil it. They were a bit repetitive but kinda fun to just relax and bust some bad dudes up. I HIGHLY recommend the DLC outfits that are available at the Legendary Outfits (gold shirt on the map) vendor. I really enjoyed the Drunken Brawler and the Monkey King outfits. They both change your fighting style, and with as much fighting as there is in this game, it helps to freshen it up. I think I got this for $10 so if you aren't sure about it, wait for a sale.

However slender can teleport which i dislike as it feels rther stupid but I like as it adds to the jumpscares factor of the game. The game is very creepy but becomes repetitive and a bit boring after a while but it is still a very good horror game and worth buying (in the sales)
